 SCCH-24 3 MVC 1393/2025  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation due to death of Roshan Khan in a road traffic accident.
2.

The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
That on 08-09-2024 at about 6-25 am., Roshan Khan was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-AK-6907 on 6th main Indiranagar 100 feet road and when he reached near Udupi Park Hotel and while taking left turn towards 12 th main Indiranagar 100 feet road, at that time suddenly the rider of Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-8886 came in a rash and negligent manner from KFC Junction towards 12th main road junction and dashed against the right back portion of the Auto-rickshaw, result of which Auto-rickshaw turtle down, result of which Roshan Khan fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately Roshan Khan was shifted to Chinmaya Mission Hospital, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient for two days.
After conservative treatment, for further management referred to Victoria Hospital, wherein even after expert treatment, Roshan Khan was succumbed to injuries on 10-09-2024 at about 9-45 pm.,
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
3. Prior to the accident, Roshan Khan was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 74 years.
He was auto driver by profession thereby, earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Due to the untimely death of Haseena vs Jeevan Kumar S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33177919/
2
Roshan Khan, petitioners are put to great mental shock and agony.

4. Respondent / the RC owner of Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-8886 has filed written statement and contended that Roshan Khan was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AK- 6907 without giving proper hand signal or indicator and he attempted to take sudden left turn and failed to notice the movement of other vehicles, result of which Auto-rickshaw swerved abruptly and came in contact with the respondent's two wheeler, result of which Roshan Khan lost balance and thrown out of auto rickshaw and sustained injuries.
The respondent further contended that he spent a sum of Rs.49,000/- towards medical expenses at Chinmaya Mission Hospital.
The respondent further contended that petitioner no.2 to 7 are all major and married children of the deceased, therefore they are not dependending on the income of the deceased.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Roshan Khan succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08-09-2024 at about 6.25 am., on 6th main Indiranagar, 100 feet road, near Udupi Park Hotel, Bengaluru,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-8886 ?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

3. What order or Award ?
6.

The respondent got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.

7. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-

sentences.text:
Issue No.1:- Petitioners have categorically contended that on 08-09-2024 at about 6-25 am.,
when Roshan Khan was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-03-AK-6907 on 6th main Indiranagar 100 feet road and when he reached near Udupi Park Hotel and while taking left turn towards 12th main Indiranagar 100 road, at that time suddenly the rider of Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-03-JV-8886 (hereinafter referred as to the offending the vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner from KFC Junction towards 12th main road junction and dashed against the right back portion of the Auto-rickshaw, result of which Auto-rickshaw turtle down, result of which Roshan Khan fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
10.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 13 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, Police intimation, Requisition submitted before the court, Spot mahazar, sketch,
Notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, IMV report, Inquest Mahazar, PM report,
charge sheet, etc., are the material documents to prove the present issue.

11. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Zammr Khan, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No 0205/2024 of Jeevan Bhima Nagar (Indiranagar) Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of B.N.S The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 281, 106(1) of B.N.S and Sec.146, 196 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: 12. The learned counsel for respondent has vehemently argued that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the deceased as he had taken left turn from 6 th main road towards 12th main road junction in Indiranagar 100 feet road without giving any direction and without observing the vehicular movement in the said road and came in contact with the offending vehicle.

It was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent that deceased too had contributed negligence hence the petitioners have to forgo compensation to the extent of negligence contributed by the deceased.

13. In the light of the argument canvassed by the Learned counsel for respondent if the police records and the evidence of PW.1 and RW.1 is perused, it is not in dispute that on the date of accident respondent was riding the offending vehicle from KFC Junction towards 12th main road junction.
It is also not in dispute that at the time of accident the deceased who was proceeding from 6th main road entered the 12th main road junction towards left side.
The width of the said road is nearly 60 feet.
There is a divider in between the road of 30 feet each.
The spot of accident is on the middle of the 30 feet road.
The respondent was proceeding in the straight road.
The deceased had already entered the vehicle on the 12th main road towards the left side.

The deceased ought to have taken all care and caution while entering the vehicle on the main road from the cross road it is only after confirming that no vehicles are passing in the main road nearby the place at which the deceased was entering the vehicle on main road, he ought to have taken the left turn.

At the same time when respondent was riding the motorcycle, on seeing the Autorickshaw entering the main road, he could have control over his vehicle and by applying brake could have avoided the accident.
Hence, it can be said that both deceased and respondent had contributed negligence.

From the spot mahazar it can be said that deceased had contributed less negligence when compared to the Haseena vs Jeevan Kumar S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33177919/
4 negligence contributed by the respondent.
Hence, the negligence contributed by the deceased is assessed at 15% and the negligence contributed by the respondent is assessed at 85%.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in Partly Affirmative.
14. Issue no 2 :
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident deceased was aged about 74 years.
In this regard, petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P12 which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 03-01- 1950.
As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2024, it can be said that deceased was aged about 74 years as on the date of accident.

15. It is contended by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 to 4 being the sons and petitioner No.5 to 7 being the daughters of the deceased are the dependents of the deceased.
16. As per the evidence of PW.1, petitioner no.2 to 7 are married and leading independent life and they are not depending on the income of the deceased.
The PW.1 further deposed that she is suffering from BP and diabetic and her children are not looking after her.
From the aforesaid evidence of the PW.1 it can be said that petitioner no.2 to 7 are not the dependents of the deceased though they are the legal representative of the deceased.

17. It is relevant to state here that during the course of trial, the learned counsel for respondent had filed application to summon the medical Officer who had conducted postmortem to prove before the court the nature of injuries sustained by the deceased and the cause for the death.

This court had rejected the said application on the ground that the injured had succumbed to the injuries within 2 days from the date of accident that too while taking treatment in the hospital and that the petitioners have produced postmortem report which discloses the cause of death.
Further neither in the written statement nor in the cross examination of PW.1 nor in the evidence of respondent they have disputed the nexus between the death and injuries sustained in the accident.

Though the learned counsel for respondent has submitted that the deceased had sustained abrasion and simple injuries but if the discharge summary and other medical records are perused, the deceased had sustained severe brain injuries.
When respondent nowhere has disputed the nexus between the death and injuries sustained in the accident there is no reason to discuss on the said point.
18. The petitioners have produced medical bills for Rs.1,10,000/- as per Ex.P18.
The respondent has categorically contended that he had paid medical expenses to the tune of Rs.46,000/-.
To evidence the said fact, the respondent has produced two advance receipt for Rs.20,000/- each as per Ex.R2 and two tax invoice as per Ex.R3 for Rs.3,000/- each.
The respondent in further has produced the Attendant's pass as per Ex.R1 and Receipt for having paid Rs.20,000/-.
It is submitted by the respondent that sum of Rs.20,000/- was paid through the account of his friend.

The Learned counsel for petitioners have disputed the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.46,000/- met by the petitioners and submitted that the medical documents relied by the respondent is in the name of deceased hence there is no reason to believe that respondent had paid the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.46,000/-.

Haseena vs Jeevan Kumar S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33177919/
5 19.
It is not in dispute that soon after the accident the deceased was shifted to the Chinamaya Hospital by the respondent.
The respondent has produced attendant's pass.
If really, respondent had not met the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.46,000/-, there was no possibility of his having Ex.R2 and Ex.R3 and it would be in the possession of the petitioners.
When Roshan Khan was the patient, it is quite natural that medical bills would be issued in the name of the patient only but not in the name of the person who bears the medical expenses.
Hence, there is every reason to believe that sum of Rs.46,000/- was paid by the respondent .
Hence, out of Rs.1,10,000/- sum of Rs.46,000/- has to be deducted and petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.64,000/- towards the medical expenses.

20. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was Auto-rickshaw driver and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the actual income and avocation of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident in question has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
21.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, and she alone is the dependant of the deceased,  of the annual income is to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining  is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
22. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 74 years no future prospect can be considered.
23. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, out of it if 50% is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, it comes around Rs.8,250/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group over 65 year is '5'.
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.4,95,000/- (Rs.8250 x 5 x 12 =4,95,000/-).
24. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband and petitioner No.2 to 7 have lost their father.

So far as the quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned, slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral Haseena vs Jeevan Kumar S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33177919/
6 expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

25. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
26.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
2 Transportation and funeral Rs. 18,150/-
expenses 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 3,38,800/-
parental
consortium

(Rs.48,400X7) 4 Loss of Dependency Rs. 4,95,000/-
5

Medical expenses Rs. 64,000/-
 Total Rs. 9,34,100/-
 26.
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.9,34,100/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
27. As regarding liability is concerned, respondent is the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
The offending vehicle was not having Insurance policy at the time of accident.

28. Since both deceased and respondent had contributed negligence to an extent of 15:85 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
The respondent being the RC owner is liable to pay 85% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
85% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.

Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.9,34,100/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Thirty Four Thousand One Hundred Only).
The Respondent is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.7,93,985/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No.II.
The respondent directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.7,94,485/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Four Thousand Four Hundred Eighty Five only) with interest within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.7,93,985/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 15% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.1,40,115/-.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.5,04,085/- Petitioner No.2 to 7 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each.
Out of the amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification through E-payment.
So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioners no 2 to 7 is concerned same is ordered to be released in their favour after due identification through E - payment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 1st day of April 2026.)
